'''Kazama Shrine''' (かざまじんじゃ) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the Kazama area of [[Nagano (city)|Nagano City]], Nagano Prefecture.

The shrine is identified as a [[Shikinaisha]].

== Overview ==
The shrine is situated approximately 3 km southeast of [[Nagano Station]], in a residential area slightly off the prefectural road [[Nagano Prefectural Road Route 34]].

Records indicate that in [[860 CE]], "Hyoubetsu Shrine" was granted Rank in the court hierarchy. In [[979 CE]], Tadanobu Yajima, a minor branch of the [[Suwa clan]], was dispatched as a steward and took the surname Kazama, marking the origins of various [[Kazama clan|Kazama clans]].

The shrine preserves a traditional lion dance known as the "Kazama Shrine Daidaikagura Lion Dance," which has been performed since [[1822 CE]]. The dance features male lions wielding swords and no lyrics. It was designated a [[Nagano City Selected Intangible Folk Cultural Property]] in [[1998|Heisei 10]].<ref>[http://bunkazai-nagano.jp/modules/dbsearch/page1166.html Kazama Shrine Daidaikagura Lion Dance] - Nagano City Cultural Heritage Database</ref>

== History ==
* [[596 CE]] (August): Mentioned in the [[Nihon Shoki]].
* [[860 CE]] (February): Recorded in the [[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]].
* [[979 CE]]: Tadanobu Yajima of the Suwa clan was dispatched as a steward and adopted the name Kazama.
* [[1697 CE]]: Renamed from Suwa Shrine to Kazama Daimyōjin.<ref>[http://weekly-nagano.main.jp/2012/01/127.html 127 Kazama Shrine: The Wind deity Renamed as a Shikinaisha] - Weekly Nagano</ref>
* [[1822 CE]] (September): Renamed Kazama Shrine by the Yoshida clan, who served as shrine administrators.
* [[1998|Heisei 10]] (August 1): The Kazama Shrine Daidaikagura Lion Dance was designated as a Nagano City Selected Intangible Folk Cultural Property.

== Access ==
* From [[Nagano Station]] (JR East and Nagano Electric Railway), take the Alpico Kōtsū (Kawanakajima Bus) Route 46 to the "Kazama" stop. The shrine is a 2-minute walk from the bus stop.
